summary: Trees are hierarchical data structures with a root node and children forming subtrees. Binary trees have at most 2 children per node. Binary Search Trees (BST) maintain the invariant: left < node < right, enabling O(log N) operations. Key traversals include inorder (left-root-right, gives sorted order in BST), preorder (root-left-right, useful for cloning/serialization), postorder (left-right-root, useful for deletion), and level-order (BFS, processes level-by-level). Most tree problems use recursion (DFS) or queue-based iteration (BFS). BST operations leverage the ordering property to prune search space.

thoughtProcess.title: 1. Identify the Tree Type
thoughtProcess.body: Is it a generic binary tree, BST, balanced tree, or complete tree? BST problems can exploit the left < node < right property to prune branches. Balanced trees have height O(log N). Complete trees can use array-based indexing (parent at i, children at 2i+1 and 2i+2).

thoughtProcess.title: 2. Choose Traversal Strategy
thoughtProcess.body: DFS (recursion or stack) for problems requiring depth-first exploration: preorder for cloning, inorder for sorted order in BST, postorder for deletion. BFS (queue) for level-by-level problems: level-order traversal, right/left view, serialize/deserialize. DFS space = O(H), BFS space = O(W) where W is max width.

thoughtProcess.title: 3. Define Recursive Subproblem
thoughtProcess.body: Most tree problems have elegant recursive structure. Ask: what do I need from left subtree? From right subtree? How do I combine them at this node? Define return type carefully (int for count/height, boolean for validation, TreeNode for construction). Base case is almost always null node.

thoughtProcess.title: 4. Exploit BST Property
thoughtProcess.body: In BST problems, use the ordering to prune: if target < node, ignore right subtree. If target > node, ignore left subtree. This reduces search space from O(N) to O(H). For validation, pass min/max bounds down recursively. For range queries, prune branches outside range.

thoughtProcess.title: 5. Handle Edge Cases Early
thoughtProcess.body: Check null root at the start. For BST, handle empty tree, single node, and duplicate values (clarify if allowed). For serialization, decide how to represent nulls (-1, 'N', etc). For deletion, cover 3 cases: leaf, one child, two children (use inorder predecessor/successor).

thoughtProcess.title: 6. Track State Across Levels
thoughtProcess.body: For BFS, process nodes level-by-level using queue size snapshot. For views (left/right), track first/last node per level. For serialization, enqueue nulls to preserve structure. For parent-tracking problems, pass parent reference or use a map.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting Null Checks
commonMistakes.why: Accessing .val on null causes NullPointerException. Always check node != null before accessing fields.

commonMistakes.title: BST Validation with Node Values Only
commonMistakes.why: BST property is global, not local. A node must be less than ALL ancestors on the right path, not just its parent. Pass min/max bounds down recursively.

commonMistakes.title: Integer Overflow in Min/Max
commonMistakes.why: If a node's value is Integer.MIN_VALUE or Integer.MAX_VALUE, the boundary check fails. Use Long to avoid overflow.

commonMistakes.title: Not Enqueuing Nulls in Serialization
commonMistakes.why: Skipping nulls loses tree structure information. Deserialization won't know where gaps are. Always enqueue children even if null, mark them as -1 in output.

commonMistakes.title: Incorrect Inorder Predecessor/Successor
commonMistakes.right:
TreeNode pred = root.left;
while (pred.right != null) pred = pred.right;
commonMistakes.why: Inorder predecessor is the RIGHTMOST node in the left subtree, not just the left child. Must traverse to the max of left subtree.

commonMistakes.title: Modifying Tree During Traversal Without Care
commonMistakes.wrong: // Deleting nodes while iterating can skip nodes or crash
commonMistakes.right: // Use postorder (process children before parent) for deletion, or mark nodes for deletion and clean up in a second pass
commonMistakes.why: Deleting a node invalidates references to its children. Process children fully before deleting parent (postorder), or collect nodes to delete and remove them afterward.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting to Return Updated Root in BST Deletion
commonMistakes.why: Deleting the root changes the tree's root. Must return the new root so caller can update their reference.

commonMistakes.title: Off-by-One in Level-Order Tracking
commonMistakes.why: Queue size changes as you add children during iteration. Capture size before loop to process exactly one level.

keyPatterns.name: DFS Recursive Template
keyPatterns.when: Any problem that can be broken into left-subtree + right-subtree + current-node logic.

keyPatterns.name: BFS Level-Order Template
keyPatterns.when: Problems requiring level-by-level processing: views, level traversal, shortest path in tree.

keyPatterns.name: BST Search/Insert/Delete
keyPatterns.when: BST operations: search in O(H), insert while maintaining order, delete with 3 cases.

keyPatterns.name: BST Validation with Min/Max
keyPatterns.when: Check if a binary tree is a valid BST. Must verify global property, not just local.

keyPatterns.name: Inorder Traversal (BST Sorted Order)
keyPatterns.when: Get sorted array from BST, find kth smallest, two-sum in BST.

keyPatterns.name: Tree Construction from Traversals
keyPatterns.when: Build tree from inorder + preorder, or inorder + postorder. Inorder splits left/right, other traversal gives root.

keyPatterns.name: Parent Tracking / Path Problems
keyPatterns.when: LCA, path from root to node, node-to-node distance. Track parent pointers or pass path down.

keyPatterns.name: BST Range Query with Pruning
keyPatterns.when: Count/collect nodes in a range [B, C]. Use BST property to skip entire subtrees.

edgeCases: Empty tree (root = null) — return base case (0, null, empty list, etc.)
Single node tree — no children, many operations trivially return the node or its value
All nodes in left subtree or all in right (skewed tree) — O(N) height, not O(log N)
Duplicate values in BST — clarify if allowed; if yes, decide left vs right placement convention
Integer overflow in BST bounds — use Long.MIN_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE for validation
Null children in serialization — must represent explicitly (e.g., -1) to preserve structure
Deleting root node — must return new root; caller needs to update reference
Leaf node deletion — simply return null; parent's pointer becomes null
Node with one child deletion — return that child; parent points directly to grandchild
Node with two children deletion — find inorder predecessor (max in left) or successor (min in right), copy value, recursively delete the pred/succ
Level-order queue size changing during iteration — snapshot size before loop to process one level
Negative node values — affects range queries and two-sum; ensure comparisons handle negatives correctly
